teachingReview.heading: Balance growth with compatibility
teachingReview.body: Preterm infants have high calcium and phosphorus needs because substantial mineral accretion normally occurs late in gestation. The amount that can be delivered is limited by solubility, final concentration, amino-acid formulation, pH, salt form, temperature, order of mixing, storage, and infusion conditions. ASPEN's compounding checklist prefers calcium gluconate when inorganic phosphate salts are used; the exact formulation still requires validation.

sourceEvidence.locator: Background/Q1 rationale: late-gestation mineral accretion interrupted by preterm birth
Prior full PDF pages1-2: formulation-specific amino-acid curves/concentrations/volume/cysteine
Prior full PDF pages1-2: mixing, electrolyte interactions and calcium-gluconate/inorganic phosphate preference
Prior complete PDF page4 section2.3 and page5 section5.2: compatibility factors/precipitation/infusion conditions

teachingReview.heading: Count both ions in phosphate products
teachingReview.body: Sodium phosphate contributes sodium and phosphate, while potassium phosphate contributes potassium and phosphate. Concentrations vary by product. Calculate mmol of phosphate and mEq of the counterion separately, then add both to the final daily electrolyte totals.

sourceEvidence.locator: Full PDF page30 / printed20 Table2: sodium and potassium contributions and product variation
Prior PDF page4 section2.4 and page5 section3 phosphate/potassium product contributions

teachingReview.heading: Use pediatric vitamin products and labeled dosing
teachingReview.body: Pediatric parenteral multivitamin dosing depends on product labeling and weight or age. An adult product is not an automatic substitute for an infant product. During shortages, use an institution-approved plan based on current ASPEN recommendations. Restore normal labeled dosing once supply returns; temporary conservation measures are not routine care.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF pages2-4: indication up to11 years, actual weight groups, preparation
PDF pages1-4: shortage-only substitutions and restore routine labeled dose after supply returns

teachingReview.heading: Adjust trace elements selectively
teachingReview.body: High gastrointestinal losses and burns can increase zinc deficiency risk; assess output, growth, skin findings, and wound healing. Copper is primarily excreted in bile, and manganese is presumed to use biliary elimination. Cholestasis therefore warrants review for copper accumulation and manganese neurotoxicity. Individualize the components instead of assuming a fixed mix fits every child or omitting all trace elements. Long-term PN without copper, zinc, or selenium can cause deficiency. Use weight, organ function, losses, duration, product content, and interpretable laboratory trends together.

sourceEvidence.locator: Full PDF pages1-2: high GI losses/burns/zinc signs, long-term omission deficiencies and monitoring
PDF pages19-20/22/25: biliary handling, cholestatic copper/manganese accumulation and individualized products

teachingReview.heading: Distinguish vitamin dose from infusion volume
teachingReview.body: INFUVITE PEDIATRIC is labeled for children up to 11 years of age. For a 2 kg child within that labeled age range under the November 2024 label, the daily single-dose preparation uses 2.6 mL from Vial 1 and 0.65 mL from Vial 2: 3.25 mL total. The pharmacy bulk package first combines both vials and supplies 3.25 mL of that mixture. These are different preparation steps, not interchangeable vial instructions. The label requires the daily dose to be added to at least 100 mL of intravenous dextrose or saline; check that volume against the complete fluid plan. Never give the product as an undiluted intravenous injection or add it directly to lipid emulsion. Verify compatibility, protect light-sensitive vitamins, and monitor vitamin status during prolonged use.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF pages2-5 sections1/2.1-2.5; Table1/Table2 for1 to<3kg:2.6+.65=3.25mL; at least100mL IV dextrose/saline, no undiluted injection/direct ILE, light protection, vitamin monitoring

teachingReview.heading: Check what a fixed trace-element mix supplies
teachingReview.body: Multrys is labeled for neonatal and pediatric patients weighing less than 10 kg who need all four supplied trace elements. Its July 2024 label uses a different schedule for 0.4 to 0.59 kg patients; do not extend the daily formula to that group. For a 1.2 kg patient, Table 1 gives 0.4 mL/day: 400 mcg zinc, 24 mcg copper, 1.2 mcg manganese, and 2.4 mcg selenium. The label's zinc total is 400 mcg/kg/day below 3 kg, or 480 mcg/day here. If no enteral zinc is received, 80 mcg/day remains to be supplied. Do not add more fixed combination simply to close a zinc gap; check individual supplementation and all routes. The label does not recommend Multrys when a patient needs less of any one component, and advises considering individual products in hepatobiliary disease.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF pages15-18/20/22/25 / Multrys printed2-5/7/9/12: under10kg/allfour ingredients,0.4-.59kg separate schedule;1.2kg Table1 .4mL at1000/60/3/6mcg/mL; zinc target400mcg/kg/day less3kg; compare all routes; lower-component/hepatobiliary restrictions

teachingReview.heading: Interpret trace-element tests in context
teachingReview.body: For long-term Multrys use, the label monitors serum zinc, copper, and selenium and whole-blood manganese. Follow the laboratory's collection and handling requirements and its reference range. ASPEN's trace-element practice tool cautions that acute illness and inflammation can distort interpretation, recommends considering inflammatory markers, and notes that serum copper does not directly measure copper balance. Combine interpretable results with intake, losses, growth, skin findings, liver function, and neurologic symptoms rather than increasing every trace element after one low result.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF page18 / Multrys printed5 monitoring: serum zinc/copper/selenium, whole-blood manganese, assay ranges/collection
PDF pages1-2 footnotes/dosing: acute illness/inflammation, CRP, serum copper not copper balance; status directs dose
